title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy option to automatically block identified external bots
summary: Hold: the briefing says the PowerShell value for automatic blocking is not documented, but Microsoft's cmdlet reference documents BlockDetectedBots. The rollout dates and opt-in default match Microsoft's notice; the feature guide and cmdlet reference also disagree about the value that disables detection.

claims.claim: Teams is extending existing external bot controls with an option to automatically block identified external meeting bots.
claims.quote: Extending the admin controls provided for managing external AI bots and regulating their access to your meetings, we are adding the option to automatically block all identified bots.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: Automatic blocking requires administrator opt-in; otherwise the current detection and participation behaviour continues unchanged.
claims.quote: Default state: Off. No changes occur unless an administrator enables the policy.

claims.claim: The new option is added to the existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: A new policy option will be added to the existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.
claims.quote: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.

claims.claim: When enabled, blocking prevents identified external meeting bots from joining meetings governed by the assigned policy.
claims.quote: Identified external meeting bots will be prevented from joining meetings governed by the assigned policy.

claims.claim: Existing bot detection and visibility remain available to organisers and administrators when blocking is enabled.
claims.quote: Existing bot detection and visibility experiences for organizers and administrators will continue to be available.

claims.claim: The notice was updated on 3 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice gives a Targeted Release rollout beginning in mid-September 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Beginning in mid-September 2026 (previously early August) and expected to complete by late September 2026 (previously late August)

claims.claim: The notice gives Worldwide General Availability beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by the end of November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The notice sets no act-by deadline and requires no action unless the organisation plans to use blocking.
claims.quote: No action is required unless you plan to use this capability.

claims.claim: The notice supplies Worldwide rollout dates but no separate GCC schedule.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

claims.claim: RequireApprovalWhenDetected is the existing default and keeps detected, marked bots in the lobby until explicitly admitted.
claims.quote: When detected, require approval before joining | *RequireApprovalWhenDetected* | (**default**) Bots are detected and marked in the lobby. They're enforced to be in the lobby until explicitly admitted into the meeting.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The feature guide documents AllowBots for Do not detect bots, under which bots are not marked and appear as ordinary external participants.
claims.quote: Do not detect bots | *AllowBots* | Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings.
claims.fix: Qualify references to AllowBots with: 'The feature guide calls this value AllowBots, but the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference lists AllowAllBots for disabling detection.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps. Do not present AllowBots as an undisputed scripting value.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The feature guide currently lists only Do not detect bots and When detected, require approval before joining, not a blocking option.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams automatically block external bots ExternalBotAccessMode block blocked lobby override; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots. Its Options table has only AllowBots and RequireApprovalWhenDetected.

claims.claim: The PowerShell value for the new automatic blocking option is not yet documented.
claims.quote: **BlockDetectedBots**: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.
claims.fix: Replace the claim that the blocking value is undocumented, including the control note and the PowerShell part of the first open question, with: 'The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference documents BlockDetectedBots for automatic blocking, although the feature guide still lists only two options.' Give the call as 'Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode BlockDetectedBots' and retain the existing cmdlet-reference citation.

claims.claim: The external bot setting is under Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: This setting is present in the Meeting Join and Lobby section of Meeting policies. Look for **"Manage external bots and their access to meetings"** and select the appropriate option.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode <value> to control external meeting bots.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy
    [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>]
... [-ExternalBotAccessMode <String>]
Controls how external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are handled when they attempt to join meetings.

claims.claim: The existing setting is a user/group meeting policy that can be configured through the default org-wide policy or targeted policies.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting bots may record or transcribe meetings without participants' awareness.
claims.quote: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting bots may store meeting data in third-party systems outside the organisation's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.claim: Teams detection uses infrastructural and behavioural signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process. We utilize a combination of infrastructural and behavioral signals

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity
claims.claim: Some external bots may evade detection, so blocking identified bots does not cover every bot.
claims.quote: Some external bots may not be detected.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Bot detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.
claims.quote: Detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.

claims.claim: With the existing lobby experience, misclassified people can be admitted and marked This is not a bot.
claims.quote: When you observe this misclassification in the meetings, you can rectify the situation by admitting the participants from the lobby and marking them with "This is not a bot" option.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether an automatically blocked participant can use the lobby correction route or receive an organiser override.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams automatically block external bots ExternalBotAccessMode block blocked lobby override; opened manage-external-bots, who-can-bypass-meeting-lobby and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. None describes an override or blocked-person lobby correction route.

claims.claim: The change adds a restriction on automated participants rather than granting an agent or automation new access.
claims.quote: we are adding the option to automatically block all identified bots.

claims.claim: The external bots feature guide does not specify the administrator role needed to edit meeting policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots automatic block ExternalBotAccessMode licensing Teams Premium blocked participant; read manage-external-bots in full. It says admins can manage meeting policies but names no administrator role.

claims.claim: Learn recommends allowing only organisers and co-organisers to admit participants from the lobby so presenters cannot admit bots.
claims.quote: Configure the meetings hosted in your organization to only allow Organizers and co-organizers to admit participants from the meeting lobby. This setting ensures that no other participant in the meeting with the presenter role can admit participants

claims.claim: Learn asks administrators to report undetected external meeting bots through Feedback in Teams.
claims.quote: Help improve the system by reporting any undetected external meeting bots to us via the Feeback option in Teams.

claims.claim: Learn lists monitoring audit logs for unusual participant activity as a best practice for managing external bots.
claims.quote: Monitor audit logs for unusual participant activity.
